title: Split Rule
description: Defines when/how an order is decomposed into sub-orders - independent of which workflow the result triggers (see workflow-trigger.schema.json) and of what happens once sub-orders complete (see completion-rule.schema.json).

condition.description: References an id in elements/split_reasons.yaml, e.g. 'storage_technology_split', 'multi_location_availability'.

split_by.description: The dimension sub-orders are split along. References an id in elements/split_dimensions.yaml - the dimensions a business splits along are open-ended, so this is a catalog rather than a closed enum, the same way condition references elements/split_reasons.yaml. tools/validate.py checks the reference.

target_override.description: Overrides the sub-order's MOVEMENT TARGET ('target'). By default this never touches 'order_target' (see order_target_override below) - use when the executing system for this sub-order can't reach the parent's target directly - e.g. an AutoStore sub-order's target is the cell's own EXIT work_center, not the parent's outbound door. Omit if the sub-order's executing system can reach the parent's target directly, so 'target' inherits unchanged too.

order_target_override.description: Overrides the sub-order's ORDER TARGET ('order_target') too, not just 'target' - the exception to order_target normally being immutable and inherited unchanged from the parent. Use only when this split_rule's destination genuinely becomes the new final business destination for the resulting sub-order, e.g. inbound putaway: the storage location a split decides is not an intermediate hop the way an outbound sub-order's target_override is, it IS where the goods are meant to end up, so target == order_target should hold once that sub-order completes. Do not use this for outbound-style splits where order_target is the customer's fixed, known-upfront destination - target_override alone is correct there. Omit for that default behavior.
